messages:
jordan: Heads-up: we have a ~3x spike in GPU Xid 79 and a smaller cluster of Xid 13s on us-west2-embed-pool between 03:12-03:18 UTC. Looks concentrated on 3 cards across 2 racks. Suspect embedder batching change from tenant 'atlas' rollout.

datadog-bot: [ALERT] gpu.xid_rate (us-west2-embed-pool) crossed threshold: 78.9/min at 2026-03-17T03:14:02Z. Top tags: xid=79,xid=13,tenant=atlas,node=gw-eu-07

jordan: Logs attached from one affected host:
```
Mar 17 03:13:58 gw-eu-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00.0): 79, Xid (0000:0000)
Mar 17 03:13:58 gw-eu-07 nvidia: GPU 0: ecc: corrected errors 102 -> 144
Mar 17 03:14:01 gw-eu-07 app[embedder]: failed batch size=8 seq=512 -> cudaMemcpyAsync err=700
Mar 17 03:14:05 gw-eu-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00.0): 13, PID 7421
```

priya: Thanks. Quick checklist: 1) confirm driver version on affected nodes 2) check if atlas changed batching/seq length around 03:10 3) check ECC counters over last 24h 4) isolate node to avoid noisy neighbor.

jordan: Driver is v535.86 on those hosts (matches fleet baseline). Atlas rollout added adaptive-batching yesterday A/B that increases avg seq length to 640 for embeddings.

casey: I'm going to cordon+drain gw-eu-07 and gw-eu-12 that show the most Xids. Will redirect atlas traffic to reserved pool.

casey: Drain commands: `rackctl drain-node gw-eu-07 --reason "xid-spike-03-17" --force`

priya: Good. While draining, can someone run the prom query for ECC and OOM signals? Suggested PromQL: `sum(rate(nvidia_ecc_corrected_errors_total{job="gpu-exporter"}[5m])) by (instance,xid)` and `sum(rate(cuda_errors_total{error_type=~"OOM|INVALID|XID"}[5m])) by (instance)`

jordan: Ran ECC query for last 6h: gw-eu-07 shows sustained small corrected ECC increases beginning ~10h ago, jumped at 03:12. Not huge but fits degraded card behavior.

casey: Action plan: 1) Drain the two nodes now (in progress) 2) Move atlas embedder traffic to reserve pool for 2hrs 3) Swap GPUs from spares when drained 4) Open HW ticket with vendor and attach ECC + Xid timeline 5) Add short-term rollback for atlas adaptive-batching

priya: Also adding an alert rule tweak: suppress transient single-xid spikes but trigger when xid_rate > 10/min for >2m and corrected_ecc grows >50 in 1h. Will push PR for alert update.

jordan: Noted. One more datapoint: NVLink errors are low and PCIe resets not observed. That points more toward memory degradation or workload pressure rather than board-level link flaps.

datadog-bot: [NOTE] Incident created: SRE-2026-0317-GPU-XID (severity: medium) by jordan. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-2026-0317

casey: I'll tag hardware ops and schedule replacement windows for tomorrow if swap confirms bad DIMM/GPU. For now keeping reserve pool active and throttling atlas batch sizes to 256 seq.

priya: After swap, we should run a stress job with varied seq lengths (128/256/512/1024) to reproduce. Also capture nv-hostengine logs and health counters.

jordan: Thanks team. Leave this thread when swaps done and mark ticket with root cause (probable ECC degradation + larger seq lengths).

casey: Done draining gw-eu-07, gw-eu-12. Atlas traffic now on reserve. Will post swap results in ticket. :white_check_mark:

priya: PR for alert rule: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/482 — please review.

jordan: Good work. Follow-ups: run stress after hardware swap, and add an atlas runbook for batch/seq rollbacks.

casey: Copy. I'll update postmortem if replacement confirms.
